messages.author: d8e75f3443fb0f5e
messages.subject: Missing data + non-normality+ mixture of ordinal and continuous data
parts:
Hello all,

I have a mixture of ordinal and continuous dataset with non-normality. Missing data is another problem. so I tried to use missing = "FIML" and weighted least square estimation

The R code I used:
## ordinal data
```{r}
sem70_scale[,c("giveUpDrivingNextYear_coded",
         "ClockDrawingScore")] <-
     lapply(sem70[,c("giveUpDrivingNextYear_coded",
         "ClockDrawingScore")], ordered)
```
```{r}
measurementmodel<- ' 
  #measurement model
  Physical_Functioning =~ b*HandStrength_avg + c*rawWalkTime
  Visual_Functioning =~ dyFarActyBoth_logMAR + depthPercep + dyContWorseEye_contrastScore_log
  Cognitive_Functioning =~ rawUFOV + rawVSA+ rawVSA+ rawVMI+ ClockDrawingScore
  Mobility =~ d*giveUpDrivingNextYear_coded + e*driverRestriction
  '
```
```{r}
fit <- cfa(model = measurementmodel, data = sem70_scale, std.lv=TRUE, missing = "FIML", ordered = c("giveUpDrivingNextYear_coded", "ClockDrawingScore"),
           estimator = "DWLS")
```
And the error message I received:
"lavaan ERROR: missing = "fiml" not available in the categorial setting"
and I also received:
"estimator = "DWLS" not available in missing = "fiml"

How should I fit my not normal, ordinal and continuous mixed dataset with missing data? Thanks a lot. 

Dan

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Missing data + non-normality+ mixture of ordinal and continuous data
parts:
Dan

FIML only works with ML estimators. You can estimate the model with a mix of items with estimator="WLSMV", or any of the WLS family
But with them you cannot use FIML. So, I would reocmmend to use multiple impuations, by first creating the imputations with the mice package, and then running them with cfa.mi() function from the semTools package

messages.subject: Re: Missing data + non-normality+ mixture of ordinal and continuous data
parts:
What do you mean by non-normal?

Non-normal in the sense of categorical data, not it will not work
Non-normal in the sense of continuous non normal, you can use it with estimator="mlr" and get adjuste fit indices and SE for the estimates, and FIML will work as well as your MLR adjustment
